stories.title: Norilsk's diesel tank spill
stories.summary: A fuel tank at a power plant near Norilsk collapsed on May 29, 2020, releasing diesel into the surrounding environment. ESA published Sentinel-2 views showing red discoloration in the Ambarnaya River on May 31 and June 1.
stories.lookFor: Open ESA's dated satellite animation to inspect the river discoloration. Use the 2020–2021 annual comparison to explore the surrounding industrial sites and river corridor; the marker is an approximate area locator, not the tank's surveyed position.
stories.limitation: The archive starts in the spill year, so Before (2020) is not a guaranteed pre-spill image. Annual mosaics may omit the plume. This view does not measure diesel extent, concentration, or cleanup success; the marker's time window is editorial, not a recovery date.

stories.title: Following the spill through time
stories.summary: A Scientific Reports study used dated Sentinel-2 images to examine the Norilsk spill, including a May 23 pre-event scene and observations from late May through July 2020. The Ambarnaya River connects the affected corridor to Lake Pyasino.
stories.lookFor: Follow the Ambarnaya corridor toward Lake Pyasino. Open the study's dated image sequence for changes during the spill, then play 2020–2025 here for longer-term landscape context.
stories.limitation: This globe shows annual optical mosaics, not the study's individual acquisitions or a processed SAR time series. Image color and later clear-looking water cannot establish pollution levels or ecological recovery. No measured contamination or cleanup layer is connected.

sources.title: Monitoring oil spill in Norilsk, Russia using satellite data

stories.title: Lake Manchar overflows
stories.summary: Extreme monsoon rainfall swelled Lake Manchar during Pakistan's 2022 floods. NASA documented the overflowing lake and surrounding inundation in early September 2022.
stories.lookFor: Inspect the lake shoreline and surrounding floodplain. Open NASA's dated satellite comparison to see the event's flood extent, then explore the annual imagery for broader landscape context.
stories.limitation: Annual cloud-free mosaics combine different acquisition dates and may exclude peak flooding. This story's map window is editorial context, not a measured flood footprint or a recovery assessment.

stories.title: A capital emerges in Borneo
stories.summary: Nusantara's construction introduced new roads, cleared areas, and government facilities into a landscape of forest and plantations. NASA documents rapid changes between 2022 and 2024.
stories.lookFor: Follow the pale road network spreading around the government core, then compare the density of cleared sites and large structures.
stories.limitation: An annual mosaic combines observations from different dates. It does not identify individual construction dates or measure forest loss by itself.

sources.title: Nusantara: A New Capital City in the Forest

stories.title: From road grids to city districts
stories.summary: Egypt's New Administrative Capital is being built east of Cairo. NASA's satellite comparisons document expanding development across the desert, including government, residential, and business districts.
stories.lookFor: Look for planned street grids filling with buildings and large facilities. New geometry is a stronger clue than changes in overall image brightness.
stories.limitation: Desert mosaics can change color with acquisition conditions and processing. A darker image is not automatically evidence of urban growth.

stories.title: A new port on reclaimed land
stories.summary: Tuas Port's first reclamation phase was completed in 2021, followed by its official opening in 2022. The project combines reclaimed land, quays, and container-terminal infrastructure.
stories.lookFor: Compare the shoreline, quay edges, and large paved yards. Distinguish newly formed land from facilities added on land that already existed.
stories.limitation: A shoreline comparison needs tidal and acquisition context. This story does not measure reclaimed area or classify land and water boundaries.

stories.title: Jasper's 2024 wildfire
stories.summary: The July 2024 Jasper wildfire affected the national park and townsite. Parks Canada documents the response and recovery. This marker locates the Jasper area, not the fire's full boundary.
stories.lookFor: Compare vegetation patterns around the town and surrounding valleys, using the official account to contextualize possible burn scars and recovery.
stories.limitation: This story does not map damaged forest. Burn severity and damaged-building counts require separate validated datasets.

stories.title: Wennington: fire at the urban edge
stories.summary: London Fire Brigade reported a major fire involving houses and scrubland in Wennington in July 2022. It is a documented example of fire affecting the edge of a city.
stories.lookFor: Use the incident report to understand the location, then inspect the surrounding settlement and vegetation across the comparison years.
stories.limitation: At approximately 10-metre resolution, annual imagery may not resolve individual damaged homes. This is a sourced event locator, not a satellite damage assessment.

stories.title: LNU Lightning Complex
stories.summary: The LNU Lightning Complex affected counties west of the Sacramento Valley in August 2020. CAL FIRE lists the complex in its incident archive, and Solano County provides recovery context.
stories.lookFor: Inspect the hills west of the valley and use the linked incident resources to distinguish the documented event from the illustrative overlay.
stories.limitation: Our archive starts in 2020, the fire year. Its annual mosaic is not a guaranteed pre-fire baseline; a true before-event analysis needs imagery from before August 2020.
